turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): In you come, Mr Keane. I've your obs done. Temperature is 37.8, pulse 88, and the blood pressure is 128 over 78.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lovely, thanks. Sit in there, the pair of you. Tell me, what's been happening?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Umm, it's the waterworks, doctor. Burning when I pass water, I'm going all the time, and me lower back is aching. Four days now, I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sounds rotten. How does the burning feel when it comes?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Like a hot sting, right at the end. Sore more than agony. And I can't hear myself think out in that waiting room, the telly's blaring, so I'm a bit scattered coming in.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): And through the night, how often are you up to the loo?
[SEG0007] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Every twenty minutes, doctor, the whole night. He wouldn't touch a bite of dinner yesterday either. I nearly had to push him in the car.
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): Ah that's not it. Three or four times, not every twenty minutes. I had toast this morning, I'm not off the food entirely. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll stick with what you're telling me so. Any nausea, or were you getting sick?
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Uh, no, I haven't felt sick.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any discharge from the penis, or blood in the urine?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): No. No discharge, and I didn't see any blood.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you been away anywhere, abroad, in the last while?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): No. House and the shops, that's it.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): And how are you in yourself? Energy, and that.
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): I feel like a wet rag since yesterday. No go in me. The back, I thought at first I'd overdone it lifting the bins, but it's just aching away.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any temperature, or shivers?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): A small bit warm last night. No shivering. I don't know how high it went.
[SEG0019] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I stay with him weeknights, I do the looking after. He takes the blood pressure tablet every morning, he doesn't miss it.
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah, the ramepril, uh ramipril, 5 mg every morning for the blood pressure. Been on it for years. And two paracetemol last night and two again this morning for the ache.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines, antibiotics or otherwise?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Nothing that I know of.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything going on with your breathing, or your chest at all?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm. No. Chest is grand.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll just feel your tummy, if that's ok. Soft, no guarding. Tender over the left loin there. Right side is fine.
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): Ow. Yeah, that's the spot. Umm, actually, err, doctor, I was queasy this morning, and it's still there a small bit. I don't know, I said no before, but it's there.

[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm glad you said. I'd say this is most likely a urine infection, with the burning, the going often, that bit of temperature and the sore loin. I won't call it definite until we see the urine.

[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll dip the urine now and send a culture to the lab. If the dip shows an infection I'll start you on co-amoxiclav, but not before that. Drink plenty of water, and I'll see you back in three days.
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): Right. Will I be grand, doctor? I don't know.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Most people settle once we treat the right bug. If you can't pass water, or you feel a lot worse, don't sit it out, ring us or go to the emergency department.
[SEG0031] person_1 (NURSE): I'll get you a sample pot on the way out, Mr Keane. Toilets are on the left there.
[SEG0032] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Come on so, we'll do that. The parking was a nightmare, but sure we're here now. Thanks, doctor.

spec.situation: Man with burning urine, frequency and lower back ache for four days; fever mild; denies discharge; no recent travel; urine test and antibiotic planned, conditional on result.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

omissions.text: Burning on urination described as a 'hot sting' occurring right at the end of passing urine, and sore rather than severe agony.
Patient denied vomiting when specifically asked if he was getting sick.
Patient initially denied nausea, then corrected this to say he was queasy this morning and still a little queasy now; the record omits the initial contradictory denial.
Nocturia detail was disputed: caregiver said every 20 minutes all night, but patient said it was 3 or 4 times overnight and the doctor would go with the patient's account.
Reduced appetite was disputed: caregiver said he would not eat dinner yesterday, but patient said he had toast this morning and was not completely off his food.
